WORKSHEET · CLASS 32 · AGES 4–5

Wash Your Hands Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A life-skills worksheet for age 4: circle the child washing hands, match toothbrushes, choose the healthy breakfast, trace WASH HANDS and draw happy faces beside good habits — on screen or on paper.

Download the sheet

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at /preschool/life-skills/wash-your-hands/ — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Find the child who washes hands BEFORE eating, and circle them.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from each child to the toothbrush that is theirs.

  3. 3

    Choose

    One breakfast is healthy and one is a treat — circle the healthy one.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the big words WASH HANDS with your favorite color.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Read every good habit and draw a happy face next to each one you do.

WHERE THIS FITS

The class behind it.

This worksheet belongs to Class 32 — Life Skills & Good Habits on the Learning Path, and the whole collection lives at /worksheets/life-skills/. One finished sheet is a full session — print it, solve it together, and let the fridge door be the gallery.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at /preschool/life-skills/care-for-clothes/ — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Look for the sparkles! Circle the clothes that are clean.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from each clothing item to its correct place.

  3. 3

    Sort

    Put each picture in a box: the clean basket or the dirty basket.

  4. 4

    Trace

    Trace the words CARE FOR CLOTHES, nice and steadily.

  5. 5

    Draw

    The washing line is half empty — draw a shirt hanging on it.
